title: Microsoft 365 Copilot: deep citations link to the cited part of Word and PowerPoint files
summary: The briefing treats an undocumented switch as proof that the service desk cannot disable deep citations; Microsoft has not established that limitation. The roadmap facts and published control path and command are supported, but two behavioural assertions need narrowing and Microsoft's Restricted Content Discovery pages disagree.

claims.where: controls[0]; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no tenant or user switch, in UI or automation, specifically for deep citations.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot "deep citations" admin settings disable Graph policy', '"deep citations" "disable"', 'Microsoft 365 Copilot deep citations Graph policySettings PowerShell setting'. Read admin settings and copilotPolicySetting; no such switch.

claims.claim: The documented Copilot settings list has no citation setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot "deep citations" admin settings disable Graph policy'. Read https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/implement/configure-copilot-admin-center, including all settings tables; no citation setting is listed.

claims.claim: The documented Microsoft Graph Copilot policy settings API supports no citation setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Microsoft 365 Copilot deep citations Graph policySettings PowerShell setting'. Read copilotPolicySetting supported IDs: copilotchatpinning, blockaccesstoopenfiles, imagegeneration, allowwebsearch, allowinadmincenters; no citation ID.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot only surfaces organisational data to which the user has at least view permissions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Copilot only surfaces organizational data to which individual users have at least view permissions.

claims.claim: Existing citations land at the top of a file rather than at the cited passage.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot citations "top" "file" verify accuracy', '"deep citation" Word PowerPoint'. Read roadmap and release-note citation passages; none states that existing links land at the top.
claims.fix: Remove 'rather than on the top of a file'. Keep the roadmap-supported statement that the planned link leads to the relevant passage.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is configured in SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites. ... Select the site you want to configure. ... Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery keeps sites out of organisation-wide search and Copilot unless the user recently interacted with them.
claims.quote: Enabling Restricted Content Discovery for each site prevents the sites from surfacing in organization-wide search and Microsoft Copilot Business Chat, unless a user had a recent interaction.
claims.fix: Replace the unqualified recent-interaction exception wherever repeated with: 'The Copilot Search FAQ describes a recent-interaction exception, but the dedicated Restricted Content Discovery page says its limits include recently interacted files and exclude experiences such as summarising an open document.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery alongside the FAQ; both are already sources.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change how citations work or are shown.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Restricted Content Discovery" "citations"'. Read restricted-content-discovery and Copilot Search FAQ; they describe discoverability and permissions, not whether citation presentation changes.
claims.fix: Replace 'it does not change how citations work' and 'it does not change how a citation is shown' with 'it affects discoverability, not access permissions', as stated at https://learn.microsoft.com/sharepoint/restricted-content-discovery.

claims.claim: The Restricted Content Discovery prerequisites include a Microsoft Copilot licence.
claims.quote: Ensure your organization has a Microsoft Copilot license. Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery updates can take time to propagate through search and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Updates can take time to propagate throughout search and Microsoft Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: The service desk cannot switch deep citations off for a user reporting a problem.
claims.quote: Searched: '"deep citations" "disable"', 'Copilot "deep citations" admin settings disable Graph policy'. Read Copilot admin settings and copilotPolicySetting; absence of a documented switch does not establish that disabling it is impossible.
claims.fix: Delete 'so the service desk cannot switch them off for a user who reports a problem'. End the sentence after 'Microsoft Learn documents no admin setting for deep citations at the time of writing (November 2026)'.

claims.claim: The roadmap description presents a link for users to follow, not an autonomous action.
claims.quote: Deep citations let users quickly verify Copilot's results by linking directly to the relevant part of the reference

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A citation is not proof that Copilot's answer is correct, and users should still verify it.
claims.quote: While we continuously improve our AI systems, AI might still make mistakes. The outputs generated may be inaccurate, incomplete, biased, misaligned, or irrelevant to your intended goals.
claims.fix: Replace 'The link shows where the text came from; it does not check Copilot's summary of it' with 'Copilot outputs may still be inaccurate, so users should read the cited passage before relying on the answer'. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/microsoft-365-copilot-application-card to sources to support that general limitation without asserting an undocumented checking mechanism.

claims.claim: Copilot settings can be inspected at Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, expand Copilot, and then select Settings.

claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to review and fix file permissions, but that control has no table row.
claims.quote: Identify SharePoint sites that hold sensitive Word and PowerPoint files with broad access, and fix their permissions with the site owners. The table contains only a deep-citations switch and Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'Identify SharePoint sites that hold sensitive Word and PowerPoint files with broad access, and fix their permissions with the site owners.' It directs a separate permissions control that has no row; do not add a new row as part of this correction.
